appeared.line: The first appearance of "Yahweh's angel" in scripture: he finds a runaway servant by a spring, and she in turn gives God a name.
appeared.quote: You are a God who sees

appeared.who: Three men — Yahweh and two angels (GEN 18:22; 19:1)
appeared.event: Three visitors at the oaks of Mamre
appeared.line: Yahweh appears to Abraham in the heat of the day as three men; Abraham runs to feed them, and from the meal comes the promise that Sarah will have a son — then two of the three turn and go on toward Sodom.
appeared.quote: He lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw that three men stood near him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth.

appeared.event: The mob blinded at Lot's door
appeared.line: The two who left Abraham reach Sodom at evening; Lot presses them into his house, the men of the city surround it, and the angels pull Lot inside and strike the crowd blind — small and great alike.
appeared.quote: They struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

appeared.event: Hagar and the boy in the wilderness
appeared.line: The second time an angel finds Hagar: the boy is dying of thirst, the angel calls from the sky, and God opens her eyes to a well.
appeared.quote: What troubles you, Hagar? Don’t be afraid. For God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.

appeared.line: At the moment Abraham raises the knife over Isaac, the angel calls his name twice from the sky and stops him.
appeared.quote: Don’t lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.

appeared.line: In a dream Jacob sees a stairway joining earth to heaven, with angels in constant traffic on it.
appeared.quote: Behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.

appeared.line: Jacob tells his wives how the angel of God spoke to him in a dream — and then spoke as the God of Bethel, the line between messenger and sender left open.
appeared.quote: The angel of God said to me in the dream, ‘Jacob,’ and I said, ‘Here I am.’

appeared.line: On the way back to Canaan the angels of God meet Jacob; he calls what he sees God's army and names the place for it.
appeared.quote: Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

appeared.line: Jacob wrestles until daybreak with one the text simply calls "a man"; Hosea 12:4 says he struggled with the angel, and Jacob himself concludes he has seen God face to face.
appeared.quote: I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.

appeared.line: The angel appears to Moses in a flame of fire in a bush that burns without being consumed; from verse 4 it is Yahweh himself who speaks.
appeared.quote: the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed

appeared.event: Between Israel and Egypt at the sea
appeared.line: The angel who went before the camp moves behind it with the pillar of cloud, standing between the two armies through the night.
appeared.quote: The angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them

appeared.line: The angel stands in the road with a drawn sword; the donkey sees him three times before God opens the prophet's own eyes.
appeared.quote: The donkey saw Yahweh’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand

appeared.line: Asked "Are you for us, or for our enemies?", the armed figure refuses both sides and tells Joshua to remove his sandals on holy ground.
appeared.quote: No; but I have come now as commander of Yahweh’s army.

appeared.line: The angel comes up from Gilgal and indicts the whole people for their covenants with the land's inhabitants; they weep, and the place is named for the weeping.
appeared.quote: But you have not listened to my voice. Why have you done this?

appeared.event: Fire from the rock for Gideon
appeared.line: The angel finds Gideon beating out wheat in a wine press, hiding it from the Midianites, and greets him as “mighty man of valor”; when Gideon brings an offering, the angel touches it with the end of his staff, fire rises out of the rock and consumes it, and he departs out of his sight.
appeared.quote: Then Yahweh’s angel stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes; and fire went up out of the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes.

seeAlso.label: The Angel of the LORD, among the named ones

appeared.line: The angel who announces Samson's birth refuses to give his name, then ascends in the flame of the altar while Manoah and his wife watch.
appeared.quote: Why do you ask about my name, since it is incomprehensible?

appeared.event: The plague stayed at the threshing floor
appeared.line: The angel sent over Jerusalem in the census plague is stopped at Araunah’s threshing floor — David sees the one who struck the people, and buys that floor; it becomes the temple mount (2CH 3:1). Chronicles sees him standing between earth and sky, drawn sword in hand (1CH 21:16).
appeared.quote: It is enough. Now withdraw your hand.

seeAlso.label: The same census, two tellings, in the fall

appeared.line: Fleeing for his life and asking to die, Elijah is woken under a juniper tree by an angel’s touch — a cake baked on coals and a jar of water, twice given — and on the strength of that food he walks forty days and forty nights to Horeb.
appeared.quote: Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for you.

appeared.line: The king has sent to Baal Zebub of Ekron about his injury; the angel sends Elijah to intercept the messengers with a death sentence instead.
appeared.quote: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you go to inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron?

appeared.event: The mountain full of fire at Dothan
appeared.line: Elisha prays for his terrified servant's eyes to be opened, and the young man sees the unseen army that was there all along.
appeared.quote: behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha

appeared.event: The night the Assyrian army died
appeared.line: In one night the angel strikes 185,000 in Sennacherib's camp, and the siege of Jerusalem ends without a battle.
appeared.quote: That night, Yahweh’s angel went out and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians.

appeared.line: Six-winged seraphim cry "Holy" above the throne, and one touches Isaiah's lips with a live coal from the altar to take his guilt away.
appeared.quote: Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!

appeared.who: Six men with slaughter weapons, and one clothed in linen
appeared.line: Ezekiel's vision of Jerusalem's judgment. The text never calls the seven angels, but they come at God's summons — one to mark the faithful, six to strike — and the killing begins at the sanctuary.
appeared.quote: set a mark on the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry over all the abominations that are done within it

appeared.who: A fourth figure in the fire
appeared.line: Nebuchadnezzar sees four men walking unharmed in the fire; he calls the fourth "like a son of the gods," and in verse 28 credits God with sending his angel — who the fourth is remains the king's description, not the narrator's.
appeared.quote: Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.

appeared.line: No one sees this one: after the night in the den, Daniel’s own testimony is that God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths — an appearance known only by its result.
appeared.quote: My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me.

appeared.event: Gabriel explains the ram and the goat
appeared.line: The first time scripture names an angel: a voice from the Ulai commands Gabriel to make Daniel understand, and Daniel falls on his face.
appeared.quote: Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.

appeared.line: While Daniel is still praying, Gabriel — one of only two angels the Hebrew Bible names — arrives at the time of the evening offering.
appeared.quote: the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening offering

appeared.event: The man clothed in linen by the Hiddekel
appeared.line: A figure like lightning and burnished bronze leaves Daniel without strength, then tells him of a twenty-one-day struggle with the prince of Persia, and of Michael's help.
appeared.quote: I have been sent to you, now.

seeAlso.label: The princes of Persia and Greece, in the demons

appeared.who: The angel who talked with me
appeared.line: Zechariah's night visions have an interpreting angel throughout; here Yahweh's angel himself pleads for Jerusalem — how long? — and is answered with comfort.
appeared.quote: O Yahweh of Armies, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah

appeared.line: The traveling companion who has guided Tobias the whole journey finally identifies himself; Tobit and Tobias fall on their faces (this book stands in the apocrypha, not the Hebrew canon).
appeared.quote: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels which present the prayers of the saints and go in before the glory of the Holy One.

appeared.event: Gabriel at the altar of incense
appeared.line: Gabriel’s first recorded sending: he stands at the right side of the altar of incense and announces John’s birth to a troubled old priest — and when Zechariah asks how he can be sure, Gabriel names himself and strikes him silent until the day.
appeared.quote: I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

appeared.line: Gabriel is sent to a virgin in Nazareth to announce the birth of Jesus; Mary answers, "Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word."
appeared.quote: Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women!

appeared.who: An angel of the Lord, in a dream
appeared.event: Joseph told not to be afraid
appeared.line: The first of three dreams: Joseph, planning to divorce Mary quietly, is stopped in his sleep — the child is of the Holy Spirit, and his name will be Jesus, “for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”
appeared.quote: Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.

appeared.who: An angel of the Lord, then a multitude of the heavenly army
appeared.line: One angel announces the birth of a Savior to night-shift shepherds, and suddenly the whole heavenly army is praising God over a field.
appeared.quote: Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.

appeared.who: An angel of the Lord, in a dream
appeared.line: The moment the magi depart, the angel comes to Joseph in sleep with a direction and a reason — Herod will seek the child to destroy him — and the family is gone to Egypt before morning.
appeared.quote: Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.

seeAlso.label: The flight to Egypt, in the Jesus room

appeared.who: An angel of the Lord, in a dream
appeared.line: Herod dies, and the angel comes a third time with the same opening words and a new direction — the third dream sends the family back to Israel.
appeared.quote: Arise and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who sought the young child’s life are dead.

appeared.line: When the devil leaves him, angels come and serve Jesus — Mark records the same ministering (MRK 1:13): the host attends the one the demons elsewhere name and flee.
appeared.quote: Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and served him.

seeAlso.label: The temptation, in the Jesus room

appeared.line: In his agony before the cross, Jesus — whom angels worship — is himself strengthened by one.
appeared.quote: An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.

appeared.line: An angel with an appearance like lightning rolls the stone from the empty tomb, sits on it, and gives the women the first Easter announcement.
appeared.quote: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said.

appeared.event: At the head and the feet
appeared.line: Mary looks into the tomb and sees two angels sitting where the body had lain; they ask why she weeps, and she answers about the missing Lord — then turns, and sees him.
appeared.quote: Woman, why are you weeping?

appeared.line: The apostles are freed and sent straight back to the temple to keep speaking; in the morning the council finds the cell locked, guarded, and empty.
appeared.quote: Go stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.

appeared.event: Philip sent to the desert road
appeared.line: An angel reroutes Philip’s ministry with a road name — south, to the desert way down from Jerusalem to Gaza — where an Ethiopian official is already in his chariot, reading Isaiah.
appeared.quote: Arise, and go toward the south to the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. This is a desert.

appeared.who: An angel of God, in a vision
appeared.event: Cornelius told his prayers were heard
appeared.line: A Roman centurion sees an angel clearly at the ninth hour; the message says his prayers and alms have gone up as a memorial before God, and sends him to fetch Peter — the door to the Gentiles opens.
appeared.quote: Your prayers and your gifts to the needy have gone up for a memorial before God.

appeared.line: The night before his execution, an angel wakes Peter in Herod's prison, his chains fall off, and the iron gate opens by itself.
appeared.quote: He struck Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Stand up quickly!” His chains fell off his hands.

appeared.line: Herod Agrippa accepts a crowd's acclaim as a god. The chapter that opens a prison for Peter ends with the king struck down.
appeared.quote: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he didn’t give God the glory.

appeared.line: Two weeks into the storm Paul reports an angel standing by him in the night with a promise: he will stand before Caesar, and everyone aboard will live.
appeared.quote: Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar.

castOut.theySaid: You are the Christ, the Son of God!
castOut.line: At sunset the whole city gathers; demons come out of many, naming him — and in both Luke and Mark he silences them, “because they knew that he was the Christ.”

castOut.place: The country of the Gadarenes, across the sea from Galilee, among the tombs
castOut.theySaid: What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me. … My name is Legion, for we are many.
castOut.line: A man no chains could hold runs to Jesus and the demons beg; permitted into a herd of about two thousand pigs, they drown it in the sea — in Matthew's account (MAT 8:29) they ask, "Have you come here to torment us before the time?"
When the demon is cast out the mute man speaks; the crowds say nothing like it has been seen in Israel, and the Pharisees first credit "the prince of the demons."

castOut.event: The blind and mute man, and the Beelzebul charge
castOut.line: Accused of casting out demons by Beelzebul, Jesus answers: "But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you" (MAT 12:28; Luke's parallel says "by God’s finger"), and speaks of binding the strong man.

castOut.place: The borders of Tyre and Sidon
castOut.line: A Gentile mother's persistence wins the only exorcism done entirely at a distance — "For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter"; Matthew adds, "Woman, great is your faith!"

castOut.place: Below the mountain of the transfiguration
castOut.event: The boy the disciples could not deliver
castOut.line: A mute and deaf spirit that has thrown a boy into fire and water since childhood defeats the disciples; the father cries "I believe. Help my unbelief!" and Jesus commands it out — "This kind can come out by nothing but by prayer and fasting."

castOut.place: The synagogue at Capernaum, on the Sabbath
castOut.theySaid: Ha! What do we have to do with you, Jesus, you Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!
castOut.line: The first exorcism in Mark: mid-sermon, an unclean spirit names Jesus before any disciple has, and is silenced and expelled with a word.
Luke records in passing that seven demons had gone out of Mary called Magdalene, who then traveled with Jesus and supported the work.

castOut.place: On the return of the seventy from their mission
castOut.line: The seventy return rejoicing that "even the demons are subject to us in your name"; Jesus answers, "Nevertheless, don’t rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven."

castOut.event: The woman bent for eighteen years
castOut.line: Jesus frees a woman with "a spirit of infirmity" who could not straighten up, calling her "a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound eighteen long years" — a release, not a rebuke-and-expulsion scene like the others.

castOut.event: The girl with a spirit of divination
castOut.theySaid: These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to us a way of salvation!
castOut.line: For many days a fortune-telling spirit advertises Paul's mission with true words, until Paul commands it out "in the name of Jesus Christ" and it leaves that very hour.

castOut.theySaid: Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?
castOut.line: Seven itinerant exorcists try to use Jesus' name secondhand; the evil spirit answers, the possessed man overpowers all of them, and they flee naked and wounded — the name is not a formula.
Jesus commands the Twelve: 'As you go, preach, saying, "The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!" Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out demons, give freely, don't charge.'

seeAlso.label: The commissioning, in the Jesus room

castOut.line: When they came down, he cast out demons which were coming out, one after another, and many were cured.

seeAlso.label: The Ethiopian, in the Acts room

castOut.line: God did extraordinary miracles by Paul's hands, so that handkerchiefs or aprons were brought from his body to the sick, and diseases left them and evil spirits went out.

seeAlso.label: The sons of Sceva, in the Acts room
